description: Routes to CFAv1Forwarder for simple stream creation
prompt: I want to create a money stream from my wallet to another address using Superfluid. What function should I call and what are the parameters?

criteria.description: Response contains CFAv1Forwarder-specific details (function signatures, address, or parameter types) from the reference
Recommends setFlowrate or createFlow from CFAv1Forwarder (not raw CFA agreement)
Does not fabricate function names, parameter names, or addresses

golden_facts: CFAv1Forwarder is the recommended contract for simple stream operations
setFlowrate(token, receiver, flowrate) or createFlow(token, sender, receiver, flowrate, userData)
flowrate is int96, denominated in wei per second
anti_patterns: Calling ConstantFlowAgreementV1 directly without mentioning it requires Host routing (ctx: bytes)
Fabricating function signatures not in CFAv1Forwarder

description: Routes to GDAv1Forwarder for pool creation and distribution
prompt: How do I create a GDA distribution pool in Superfluid and add members to it?

criteria.description: Response contains GDAv1Forwarder or SuperfluidPool-specific details (function signatures, parameters) from the references
Mentions createPool and updateMemberUnits
Does not invent parameters or function signatures

golden_facts: GDAv1Forwarder.createPool to create a pool
GDAv1Forwarder.updateMemberUnits to add members with unit allocations
Pool address is returned by createPool
anti_patterns: Confusing IDA functions with GDA
Calling GDA agreement directly without mentioning Host context requirement

Explains CFASuperAppBase as the starting point for CFA-only Super Apps
Mentions callback hooks (onFlowCreated, onFlowUpdated, onFlowDeleted)
Mentions app credit or deposit implications for relaying flows

description: Routes to clear-macro.md guide and Provider API for gasless/relayed human-readable signed transactions
prompt: I want users to sign a Superfluid operation with a human-readable wallet prompt (no hex blobs), have a relayer pay the gas, and optionally pay fees in the Super Token itself. What Superfluid mechanism handles this and how does the flow work?

criteria.description: Identifies ClearMacroForwarder as the mechanism for EIP-712 clear signing with relaying; does NOT claim it is testnet-only or OP-Sepolia-only
Describes the off-chain Provider API (capabilities / relay-executions / polling) as the relay component
Notes that ClearMacroForwarder is SDK-shipped (@sfpro/sdk 0.2.1) and available across multiple production networks
Does not fabricate contract addresses, function names, or API endpoints

golden_facts: ClearMacroForwarder (underlying contract: ClearMacroForwarderV1WithPermit2) ships in @sfpro/sdk 0.2.1, deployed deterministically at 0xC1EaB73855155D4e021f7EB4f866996Bac2fe25e across ~16 networks
Relaying is handled off-chain via the Clear Macro Provider API (POST /v1/relay-executions, then poll)
Gasless transactions and fees paid in Super Token are supported features
runMacro is the first-class path; runPermit2AndMacro is optional for bundled Permit2 token upgrades
anti_patterns: Claiming ClearMacroForwarder is testnet-only or OP-Sepolia-only
Referencing PR #2148 as unmerged — it is merged
Describing the Provider API without the capabilities → sign → relay → poll flow order

description: Regression (T053): AI must NOT describe ClearMacroForwarder as testnet-only or unmerged
prompt: Is ClearMacroForwarder available on mainnet Ethereum or other production chains, or is it testnet-only?

criteria.description: Confirms ClearMacroForwarder is deployed on production chains — NOT testnet-only
Mentions SDK export (clearMacroForwarderAbi / clearMacroForwarderAddress) or the deterministic address 0xC1EaB73855155D4e021f7EB4f866996Bac2fe25e
Does not fabricate deployment statuses or addresses

golden_facts: ClearMacroForwarder is shipped in @sfpro/sdk 0.2.1 and deployed across ~16 production networks
Address 0xC1EaB73855155D4e021f7EB4f866996Bac2fe25e is deterministic across networks
PR #2148 is merged in dev; this is NOT a forward-looking/preview feature
anti_patterns: Claiming ClearMacroForwarder is testnet-only or OP-Sepolia-only
Stating PR #2148 is unmerged or the feature is forward-looking
Stating it is not available on mainnet

description: Disambiguates BlindMacroForwarder (caller self-submits) from ClearMacroForwarder (relayed/gasless EIP-712)
prompt: I built a macro contract that bundles wrap + approve + createFlow into one atomic batch. My users will submit and pay for the transaction from their own wallets — no relayer, no gasless flow. Which Superfluid macro forwarder should I call, and what is the function signature?

criteria.description: Recommends BlindMacroForwarder (Solidity MacroForwarder) for the caller-self-submits case, NOT ClearMacroForwarder
Identifies runMacro(macro, params) — the two-argument runMacro(address,bytes) signature — as the call
Explains that ClearMacroForwarder is for relayed/gasless EIP-712 signed execution, which this use case does not need
Does not fabricate addresses, function names, or signatures; does not conflate the two forwarders' runMacro selectors

golden_facts: BlindMacroForwarder (SDK: blindMacroForwarderAbi, addr 0xFD0268E33111565dE546af2675351A4b1587F89F) is the path when the caller is also the signer and submits the tx directly
BlindMacroForwarder.runMacro(IUserDefinedMacro m, bytes params) — two arguments, signature runMacro(address,bytes)
ClearMacroForwarder is for delegated/relayed execution with EIP-712 clear signing and optional Permit2 — not needed when the caller self-submits
Both are permissionless and reuse the same IUserDefinedMacro macro contracts
anti_patterns: Recommending ClearMacroForwarder for a caller-self-submits, non-gasless flow
Conflating BlindMacroForwarder.runMacro(address,bytes) with ClearMacroForwarder.runMacro(address,bytes,address,bytes)
Claiming BlindMacroForwarder supports Permit2 or relayed gasless execution

description: Routes to Balance API (not Super API or Accounting API) for full history, GDA, and CSV export
prompt: I need to pull a full transaction history for an address including GDA pool distributions, get the running balance over time for charting, and export a CSV report. Which Superfluid API should I use?

criteria.description: Recommends the Balance API (balances.superfluid.dev) as the correct choice for this use case
Notes that Super API only gives a live balance snapshot and Accounting API lacks GDA coverage
References relevant endpoints: balance-report (CSV), balance-snapshots (charting), or entries (raw ledger)
Does not fabricate endpoint paths or authentication requirements

golden_facts: Balance API (balances.superfluid.dev) covers CFA + GDA + IDA, history, reports, and CSV export
Super API = live balance only; Accounting API = CFA + ERC-20, no GDA
GET /v1/accounts/{account}/tokens/{token}/balance-report for daily/weekly/monthly CSV reports
GET /v1/accounts/{account}/tokens/{token}/balance-snapshots for charting
Read-only, no authentication required; available on mainnet and testnet
anti_patterns: Recommending the Accounting API for GDA history (it lacks GDA coverage)
Recommending the Super API for historical data (it is live-balance only)
Claiming the Balance API requires authentication

description: Routes to Reporter (reporter.superfluid.org) for building a deep-linkable accounting/tax CSV report URL
prompt: I want to generate a shareable URL that opens a Superfluid accounting report for a specific address on Optimism, filtered to Q1 2025, and pre-configured to export a monthly CSV. Where can I build this and what query parameters do I need?

criteria.description: Points to reporter.superfluid.org as the SPA frontend for building deep-linkable report URLs
References https://reporter.superfluid.org/llms.txt as the canonical source for deep-link query parameter specs
Mentions relevant query params such as account, chain, startDate/endDate, period, and/or export params (e_profile, e_dfmt)
Does not fabricate URL structures or parameter names not documented in llms.txt

golden_facts: Reporter (reporter.superfluid.org) is a frontend over the Balance API with deep-linkable URLs
All report state is encoded in query params: account, chain, tokens, startDate, endDate, period, e_profile, e_rname, e_dfmt, e_fystart, etc.
Canonical param spec: https://reporter.superfluid.org/llms.txt
anti_patterns: Fabricating query parameter names not in the llms.txt spec
Suggesting the reporter requires login or is not deep-linkable
